description_full: Elis SA provides flat linen, workwear, and hygiene and well-being solutions in France, Central Europe, Scandinavia, Eastern Europe, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Latin America, Southern Europe, and internationally. It offers accommodation, catering, and healthcare and social linens; workwear and personal protective equipment; beverage solutions, such as bottled water cooler, coffee bean machine, networked water cooler, and pod coffee machine; floor protection mats and mops; industrial wipers; and pest and rodent control, insect control, or disinfection services. The company provides washroom hygiene services, such as hand washing and drying, toilet hygiene and urinals, lavatories, and air fragrancing; and reusable cleanroom garments, footwear, goggles, and equipment solutions, as well as cleaning systems. In addition, it offers various solutions for collection and disposal of infectious waste. The company serves the catering, accommodation, healthcare and social welfare, industries, trade and retail, and services sectors, as well as public authorities and administration. The company was founded in 1883 and is headquartered in Saint-Cloud, France.

financial_summary: ELIS is a mid-cap industrials business with a $5.3B market cap on $5.3B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +10% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 6% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 33%.

The business throws off $691M in free cash flow — roughly 13 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 4.12× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -12.0% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.3× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 4.0×.

Management returns a meaningful 5.2% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 21% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
